literal: By hostility will arise unpleasant things all; by friendliness will arise great goodness which is called abundance.
translation: All painful things arise from hostility; from friendliness arises the great wealth called goodness.
modern: பகையினால் துன்பங்கள் எல்லாம் உண்டாகும்; நட்பினால் நன்னயம் என்று சொல்லப்படும் பெருஞ்செல்வம் உண்டாகும்.
explanation: This couplet contrasts the consequences of hostility (ikal) and friendliness (nakal). The author explains that all painful and unpleasant experiences (iṉṉāta ellām) in life are born out of harboring hostility. Conversely, cultivating friendliness and joy with others yields the ultimate abundance (cerukku) which is supreme goodness (naṉṉayam). Here, 'nakal' refers to a cheerful, friendly disposition, and 'cerukku' is used in the sense of a rich abundance of virtue.
